sentences.text:
1. Present appeal is under Section 29 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 against the order dated 28.01.2023 (hereinafter referred to as impugned order) passed by Ld. MM,
Mahila Court, North, allowing the interim maintenance of Rs.5000/- per month (Rs. Five Thousand only) to the respondent/ complainant (in the main case).

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Amit Dahiya Vs. Vinita Page no. 1 of 4 2.

It is submitted by ld. Counsel for appellant that the ld. MM without appreciating submission of the appellant in the case has wrongly passed the impugned order in a mechanical manner without appreciating the evidence.
It is further submitted that appellant has no earning income since 2018 due to Schizophrenic disorders and appellant himself is dependent on his mother's pension income to bear his personal expenses.
It is further submitted that respondent is well qualified MCA and able to maintain herself, working as a teacher in a private school.
Amit Dahiya vs Smt. Vinita on 3 June, 2023

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84187271/
1 3.
It is submitted by ld. Counsel for respondent that there is no illegality in the impugned order.
It is submitted that complainant has no source of income and it is denied that she is a professional MCA.

It is further denied that respondent is working in a private school and also giving private tuitions.
4.
Brief facts of the case are that the complainant got married to appellant Amit Dahiya 23.04.2015 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies.

It is further alleged that soon after marriage, she was subjected to cruelty at the hands of her husband (appellant) and his family members for demand of dowry and also her stridhan was misappropriated which was not returned despite specific demand and the complainant had filed criminal cases under Section 498A/406/34 IPC, under Section 12 D.V. Act and the application under Section 23 D.V. Act.
Amit Dahiya Vs. Vinita Page no. 2 of 4 5.
I have heard the arguments from both the parties and duly persused to the record.
6. The argument during the trial raised by the appellant that he was suffering from Schizophrenic disorders and certain medical documents have already been filed before Ld. Trial Court.

So far,
there is no definite finding by a constituted a Medical Board that the appellant is sufferiing from Schizophrenia and in the medical documents filed along with the appeal, reflects that he merely has depression and mood swings.

Taking lenient view, the Ld. Trial Court has infact ordered that a meagre maintenance of Rs.5000/- per month be awarded which is even less than the minimum wages as per the government notification duly considering the totality of the facts and circumstances.
Appellant as such shall have due opportunity to take his defence during the course of trial.

7. At this initial stages and the available material on record, from the totality of facts and circumstance of the case and considering the aforesaid discussion, there appears to be no illegality in the impugned order passed by Ld. Magistrate, Mahila Court dated 28.01.2023 and the same is upheld, accordingly.
The appeal being devoid of any merits is dismissed.
8. Parties are directed to appear before Ld. Trial Court on 15.07.2023.
Amit Dahiya Vs. Vinita Page no. 3 of 4 9.
Trial Court Record be sent back along with copy of this judgment.
10. Appeal file be consigned to record room.

Pronounced in open (SHEFALI SHARMA)

 NORTH DISTRICT,
